h2: Plumber Kuta & Legian – One Person, Full Fix at Your Villa
intro: A leaking tap in a Legian guesthouse or a blocked drain on Jl. Padma doesn't wait for a dispatch team. When you book this Plumber Kuta & Legian service, I come myself with the right parts, trace the fault through decades-old pipework, and leave the job finished. Villas, small hotels and apartments along the beachfront are my daily route.

sections.text: Kuta and Legian are Bali's oldest tourist corridors, so much of the pipework beneath these streets has been in continuous service for decades. Septic lines shift, internal pipe walls thin out, and the low-lying lanes around Kuta Beach regularly flood when monsoon rains hit, forcing water back up through floor drains. Layer in the salt-heavy air rolling off the beach and metal fittings corrode far sooner than they would inland. Blockages, weeping joints and seized valves dominate the calls I get here more than anywhere else on the island.

sections.h3: Typical Jobs Across Kuta, Tuban & Legian
sections.text: In a three-bedroom villa on Jl. Padma or a ten-room guesthouse in Tuban, wear hits differently. Mixers seize after months of hard water, cistern floats fail one bathroom after another, and washing-machine hook-ups leak at the connection point within a season. My work ranges from swapping a corroded trap under a basin to installing an entire new toilet with its supply line, re-piping a hot-water circuit, or connecting a dishwasher where none existed before. I bring the parts; you don't need to source anything.

sections.h3: Send Photos on WhatsApp for a Quote
sections.text: Before I head over, send two or three photos on WhatsApp: the leaking fitting, the pressure gauge if you have one, or the drain that's backing up. A short video of the running cistern helps too. Tell me which street you're on — Kuta, Legian, Tuban — and whether it's a ground-floor or upper-floor unit. From those images I can usually identify what part is failing and reply with a fair quote for the job. No obligation, no call centre, just a direct message back.

sections.h3: Keeping Fittings Alive in Salt Air
sections.text: A few habits stretch the life of your plumbing in this coastal zone. Flush mixer cartridges every six months so mineral build-up doesn't lock them shut. Check the rubber seals inside your cistern quarterly — they're inexpensive to replace and stop most running-toilet calls. If your villa sits near Kuta Beach, wipe exposed metal fittings monthly with a dry cloth to slow salt corrosion. After any heavy rain, run all taps for a minute to clear sediment that flooding pushes into the lines.

faq.q: Do you carry common parts with you?
faq.a: Yes — mixers, traps, hoses, cistern floats and standard fittings travel in my kit, so most single-fault jobs are done in one visit. For anything larger like a full pipe replacement, I'll confirm the exact part before heading out.

faq.q: Can you handle a guesthouse with multiple bathrooms?
faq.a: Absolutely. I work through each bathroom systematically, fix what's failing, and note anything else close to wearing out so you can plan replacements rather than dealing with them room by room.

faq.q: How do I get a quote?
faq.a: Send photos or a short video on WhatsApp along with your street name. I'll look at the images, tell you what I think is wrong, and reply with a price for the repair.
